items.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>As a 100% atom-economy process, direct oxidation of methane into methanol remains as a grand challenge due to the dilemma between activation of methane and over-oxidation of methanol. Here, we report that water enabled mild oxidation of methane into methanol with >99% selectivity over Au single atoms on black phosphorus (Au<jats:sub>1</jats:sub>/BP) nanosheets under light irradiation. The mass activity of Au<jats:sub>1</jats:sub>/BP nanosheets reached 113.5 μmol g<jats:sub>catal</jats:sub><jats:sup>−1</jats:sup> in water pressured with 33 bar of mixed gas (CH<jats:sub>4</jats:sub>:O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> = 10:1) at 90 °C under light irradiation (1.2 W), while the activation energy was 43.4 kJ mol<jats:sup>−1</jats:sup>. Mechanistic studies revealed that water assisted the activation of O<jats:sub>2</jats:sub> to generate reactive hydroxyl groups and •OH radicals under light irradiation. Hydroxyl groups reacted with methane at Au single atoms to form water and CH<jats:sub>3</jats:sub>* species, followed by oxidation of CH<jats:sub>3</jats:sub>* via •OH radicals into methanol. Considering the recycling of water during the whole process, we can also regard water as a catalyst.</jats:p>
title: Water enables mild oxidation of methane to methanol on gold single-atom catalysts

items.abstract:
<jats:title>Abstract</jats:title>
                  <jats:p>
                    Oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is essential for electrochemical water splitting and renewable hydrogen production. Ruthenium‐based catalysts exhibit excellent performance but suffer from insufficient stability to practical application. Herein, a spin‐state engineering strategy is explored to modulate the spin‐electron distribution of Ru single atoms via the intrinsic magnetism of Mn
                    <jats:sub>5</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>8</jats:sub>
                    substrate for efficient acidic OER. In Ru─Mn
                    <jats:sub>5</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>8</jats:sub>
                    system, the favorable Ru
                    <jats:sup>4+</jats:sup>
                    ‐O‐Mn
                    <jats:sup>2+</jats:sup>
                    configuration facilitates Ru‐site spin polarization and drives Ru
                    <jats:sup>4+</jats:sup>
                    from low‐spin to high‐spin through strong ferromagnetic coupling, whereas Ru
                    <jats:sup>4+</jats:sup>
                    remains low‐spin in nonferromagnetic Ru─MnO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    . Unpaired d
                    <jats:sub>π</jats:sub>
                    electrons of high‐spin Ru
                    <jats:sup>4+</jats:sup>
                    enhance π‐donation to coordinated O
                    <jats:sup>2−</jats:sup>
                    , optimizing Ru─O orbital overlap. Moreover, the interaction between high‐spin Ru
                    <jats:sup>4+</jats:sup>
                    and key intermediates is strengthened. Consequently, Ru─Mn
                    <jats:sub>5</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>8</jats:sub>
                    achieves a low overpotential of 186 mV at 10 mA cm
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    and sustains stability over 160 h at 100 mA cm
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    in acidic medium, outperforming Ru─MnO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    (440 mV, 30 h) and commercial RuO
                    <jats:sub>2</jats:sub>
                    (250 mV, 40 h). When applied as an anode in a proton exchange membrane water electrolyzer, Ru─Mn
                    <jats:sub>5</jats:sub>
                    O
                    <jats:sub>8</jats:sub>
                    realizes 1 A cm
                    <jats:sup>−2</jats:sup>
                    at 1.68 V and maintains stable operation for over 50 h. This work proposes a ferromagnetic interaction‐driven spin modulation strategy, offering a robust pathway for designing high‐performance electrocatalysts for acidic water oxidation.
                  </jats:p>
title: Intrinsic Ferromagnetism Coupling‐Driven the Spin Reconfiguration of Single‐Atom Ru for Enhanced Acidic Water Oxidation
